name_note: The genus is named for its only cultured species, Pararoseburia lenta; most other genomes GTDB places here are uncultured and carry NCBI labels such as Roseburia or Pseudobutyrivibrio.

sentences.text: Pararoseburia lenta is a strictly anaerobic, motile bacterium that was isolated from human faeces.
Its cells are Gram-negative, non-spore-forming, non-pigmented and spiral-shaped or slightly curved rods carrying flagella.
The species was proposed as the type of a new genus forming a distinct lineage in the family Lachnospiraceae.
The reported end products of glucose fermentation are acetate, propionate, iso-butyrate, butyrate and valerate.
Pararoseburia lenta was later reported as the closest relative, at 92.2% 16S rRNA gene similarity, of anaerobic strains isolated from pig faeces.
